sentences.ko: 그러니까 내가 노래 부르다가 중간에 재채기하더라도 일부러 그러는 거 아니야.
sentences.text: So if I sneeze in the middle of a song, it's not on purpose.

alts.text: Heads up, if I sneeze mid-song, I'm not doing it on purpose.
Should I sneeze during a song, please understand that it is not intentional.

sentences.note: **on purpose**는 '일부러'라는 뜻으로, 변명하거나 사과할 때 'I didn't do it on purpose.'처럼 아주 자주 씁니다. **in the middle of**는 '한창 ~하는 도중에'라는 말로, 뭔가 하다가 끊길 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 나이가 어느 정도 되면 룸메이트랑 사는 건 좀 처량한 것 같아.
sentences.text: I think you reach a certain age, having a roommate is just kind of pathetic.

alts.text: Past a certain age, roommates are kinda sad.
In my opinion, once a person reaches a certain age, living with a roommate is somewhat pathetic.

sentences.note: **reach a certain age**는 나이를 콕 집지 않고 '나이가 좀 들면'이라고 돌려 말할 때 씁니다. **kind of pathetic**처럼 kind of를 붙이면 '좀 한심하다'로 말이 부드러워집니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 근데 내가 면접 보던 식당에 하필 우리 사장님이 와 있어서 다 들어 버렸어.
sentences.text: Well, my boss was at the same restaurant where I was having my interview and he heard everything.

alts.text: Turns out my boss was at the same place as my interview. Heard the whole thing.
Unfortunately, my employer was at the restaurant where my interview took place, and he overheard all of it.

sentences.note: **the same restaurant where**처럼 'the same + 장소 + where'로 '바로 그 장소에'를 말합니다. **he heard everything**은 들키면 안 될 말을 누가 다 들었을 때 '다 들었어'라고 하는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리 사귄 지 이제 겨우 2주쯤밖에 안 됐어.
sentences.text: We've only been going out a couple of weeks.

alts.text: It's only been, like, two weeks.
It has only been a couple of weeks since we started dating.

sentences.note: **going out** 은 '사귀다'라는 뜻으로 아주 흔하게 써요. 사귄 지 얼마 안 됐다고 말할 때 **a couple of weeks** 를 붙여 '2주쯤'이라고 대충 말하면 자연스러워요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너 없으면 나 진짜 어떻게 하지.
sentences.text: I don't know what I'm going to do without you.

alts.text: I honestly cannot imagine what I would do without you.

sentences.note: **I don't know what I'm going to do without you** 는 떠나는 사람에게 아쉬움을 전하거나 크게 도와준 사람에게 고마움을 표현할 때 써요. 작별 인사나 감사 인사에 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니, 난 우리가 망칠 만한 사이라고 생각도 안 했어.
sentences.text: Look, I didn't think there was a relationship to jeopardize.

alts.text: Hey, I didn't know we were even a thing.
To be honest, I did not believe there was a relationship that could be put at risk.

sentences.note: **Look,** 은 해명하거나 반박을 시작할 때 '저기, 있잖아' 하고 앞에 붙이는 말이에요. **jeopardize** 는 '위태롭게 하다'라는 뜻이고, 관계나 일자리를 망칠 수 있다고 말할 때 자주 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 응, 걔네도 꽤 미안해하는 것 같긴 하더라.
sentences.text: Yeah, they do seem to feel pretty bad.

alts.text: Looks like they feel pretty awful.
It does appear that they feel quite bad about it.

sentences.note: **do seem** 처럼 seem 앞에 do를 넣으면 '정말 그래 보이긴 해'라고 힘을 주는 말이 돼요. **feel pretty bad** 는 잘못한 사람이 미안해하거나 죄책감을 느낄 때 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends
